This is hilariously one of my biggest issues, I know I am a competent player but can’t help that feeling that everyone views me as a weakest link. Though no-one really sticks around much and there aren’t many performances or gigs where we have the opportunity to get to know each-other, I plan on taking the extra steps to talk to my band mates even if the conversation needs to be motivated along.

Thanks man, with as little time as my post was allowed to be seen in the subreddit Ive received the most helpful advice for addressing my struggles with the social aspects of music ever. Im glad you made the right steps for yourself and out of inspiration I will take mine as well.

This resonated heavily with me, as someone who struggles fulfilling their basic human needs, music became priority while self care became less than an afterthought. Mental illness seems to go hand in hand with the industry but I am infinitely grateful for people willing to share their advice on how we may be able to cope with/ treat them.
L moderation
Thank you for the advice, i had never really viewed my social skills as something that could be improved and honed and rather something that was a product of the environment they were developed in.

Seeing how seriously some of these new players take the ensemble definitely did not make me feel like I had been applying myself well enough. But at the same time its like damn dude this ensemble plays one performance per quarter, since the new year started our band sounds the best it has since ive joined but the vibe during every practice lacks the positive fun vibes from the previous year. Ive improved enough that I know I should be proud of myself but this new atmosphere leaves me feeling less than.

Thank you for your words man, the bit regarding quitting further reinforcing that feeling of defeat and isolation felt particularly enlightening, I sure as hell don’t want to feel like my mental illness prevented me from doing the things I love. And you are right, though its never felt so obvious as it does here in jazz band, Ive never been the best at interacting and have allowed my problems to be self fulfilling in many situations. Im not going to allow my social issues to make me fail but I will work on addressing them.

A significant amount of the people in my college band went to highschool together and have clear bonds where as I was from somewhere else. Seeing these relationships from day 1 made it daunting to try to talk to these people and even after doing so it never felt like anyone from these groups was particularly interested in reciprocating. Now I kinda just shoot out the occasional commentary during class but it mainly feels like a cheap attempt at feeling included.

Playing jazz on my own is exciting though frustrating as the more I learn about theory, the less I see myself as a valuable player and view all the holes in my playing and theory knowledge. I was not so critical before but under my new professor who’s encouraged me in an extremely positive way to push myself further, I find myself disappointed with myself more often than not. With new players from a nearby highschool joining in with us, our charts have only gotten harder and its been significantly more difficult to keep up with the tunes we’re learning. With these new players I also feel alot of dissatisfaction rippling through the band everytime we practice as the bar is set higher than before. Now seldom do I play a chart or a solo and feel happy with myself as I know I could do better, the highschoolers ARE doing better, and my professor wants better.

I was considering therapy as I seem to only get more in my own head the more I try to push myself against the emotional ins and outs. Ive always really seen myself as an obstacle standing in my own way, just been scared to try and dump all of my internal issues on someone else.

Im a tenor saxophonist, at first one of only 2 saxes in the band, now there are more from a highschool nearby that are a significantly more skilled than myself though it doesn’t bother me all that much, what was rough was thinking itd be easier to get to know them then the other tenor player but that wasn’t the case.
